meta.title: The ecentic platform: connect, simulate, fix, sell, track
meta.description: Connect your catalog, compare products with AI models, publish changes you choose, test agent checkout and track detected Shopify referrals.

overview.title: Everything a store needs to sell through AI.
overview.description: Five steps, in order. Connect your catalog, see how AI models compare it, improve the data they read, test the path to checkout and track what you can observe. You choose what to publish and when to rescan.

sections.title: Your catalog, in one place. Product content stays in your control.
sections.description: Your catalog, in one place. Shopify, WooCommerce, a supported product feed or CSV. Import product data first; choose publishing separately.

items.title: Shopify app
items.body: Connect through Shopify OAuth. Product imports do not rewrite your listings. Connecting also installs the Shopify visit-tracking script.
items.label: Explore

items.title: WooCommerce plugin or REST API
items.body: Connect with the ecentic plugin or REST API keys. Publishing needs write permissions; a read-only key can import products.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Product feeds
items.body: Import supported RSS/XML feeds or JSON product arrays, including products or items collections. The feed must fit the supported mapping and the 10 MiB limit.
items.label: Explore

items.title: CSV upload
items.body: Start from a spreadsheet export using the importer’s supported columns. This does not connect a write-back channel to the original platform.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Import from a store address
items.body: Start with an accessible public Shopify or WooCommerce catalog. You create an account before the catalog is imported. Password-protected or unsupported catalogs need another connection method.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Google Merchant Center
items.body: Connect separately for Shopify stores. Read diagnostics, prepare supplemental data and choose when to send published fixes.
items.label: Explore

sections.title: See how AI shops your catalog. Product by product.
sections.description: See which products the models pick, and why. ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini compare your product with a named competitor and record their reasoning.

items.title: Agent simulations
items.body: Controlled product comparisons on ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. A scan groups the comparisons you request.
items.label: Explore

items.title: AI win rate
items.body: Break down completed simulated decisions by product, model and competitor. It is not a live market-share or sales measure.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Competitor battlecards
items.body: Inspect the recorded comparison and the strengths or gaps described by the model. Check any suggested product fact against your own source data.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Agent replay
items.body: Follow the reasoning recorded during a simulation. This is the model’s explanation, not a recording of a shopper’s session.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Agent readiness audit
items.body: Check AI crawler rules in robots.txt, Product JSON-LD in sampled page HTML, product identifiers, content depth and generated-feed eligibility. Pages that cannot be fetched are reported as warnings. The audit does not execute a browser or certify that no bot wall exists.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Listing quality check
items.body: Run 34 rules based on Google’s and OpenAI’s feed specifications against supported fields in active imported products. The checks include identifiers, brand and required listing information.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Brand Visibility
items.body: The dashboard feature asks ChatGPT a set of brand questions. Its current coverage is ChatGPT, separate from the three-model product scan.
items.label: Explore

sections.title: Fix the data AI reads. Publish when you are ready.
sections.description: Rewrite titles and descriptions from existing facts. Publish structured data separately and choose when to send published fixes to Merchant Center on Shopify.

items.title: Listing rewrites
items.body: Apply generates and publishes title and description changes on directly connected Shopify or WooCommerce stores. Rewrites reorganize existing facts. Confirm missing facts in your source catalog first.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Structured data
items.body: Publish schema.org Product data through a separate action. Shopify stores need the app embed enabled for the product metafield to render; the WooCommerce plugin renders its product metadata.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Missing attributes
items.body: Simulations and listing checks can surface gaps. ecentic does not generate GTINs, certify product claims or manufacture specifications you do not have.
items.label: Explore

items.title: You choose when each change is published.
items.body: For a listing rewrite, Apply is the publishing action. Structured data uses a separate publishing action. You can also choose an explicit bulk action for the products it covers.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Send published fixes to Merchant Center.
items.body: On Shopify, send the published fixes through the Google Shopping controls. This creates supplemental data without replacing the main feed. Listing Apply does not automatically run this sync.
items.label: Explore

sections.title: Let AI check out. On your terms.
sections.description: Test what an agent meets at checkout. On WooCommerce, provide a path to cart and orders using your store’s gateway and configured access controls.

items.title: Agent checkout on WooCommerce
items.body: Expose product search, real carts and checkout through the ecentic plugin and hosted endpoints. Orders belong to your store. Access controls are configurable: an empty allow-list permits all platforms, and signatures are mandatory only when that option is enabled.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Sell inside ChatGPT
items.body: Coming soon. Publication of the ecentic app in ChatGPT’s app directory has not been confirmed. Product simulations are available separately.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Checkout playground
items.body: Run a test agent against your store tools. Ten anonymous messages are available; use a staging store for checkout tests.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Checkout validator
items.body: Fetch a store’s discovery profile and inspect the reported checks. A validation result does not enroll the merchant in an AI platform’s program.
items.label: Explore

items.title: WebMCP scanner
items.body: Inspect source evidence of tools and forms across a small sample of pages. The scanner does not execute browser tools or submit forms.
items.label: Explore

sections.title: See what AI sends you. Store by store.
sections.description: See detected AI referrals on Shopify. Request new scans after your changes, and keep visits separate from simulated results and estimates.

items.title: AI traffic on Shopify
items.body: Recognizes referral domains for ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot and You.com, plus known user-agent signals. It requires the browser script and available signals; it does not observe every non-JavaScript crawler or identify every direct visit.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Estimated lift per fix
items.body: Lift is an estimate recorded with the listing change. It is not measured revenue or a completed post-publish experiment.
items.label: Explore

items.title: Rescans you request
items.body: Run a new scan when you want to compare products again. Scheduled rescans are not active today.
items.label: Explore

items.title: All your stores in one account
items.body: The multi-store hub holds stores owned by one account. It does not provide team seats, delegated agency access or single sign-on.
items.label: Explore

items.title: API, MCP server and CLI
items.body: Developer tools support discovery, plans, connection and onboarding workflows. The current public interfaces do not export dashboard scan results or visit tracking data.
items.label: Explore

sections.title: What ecentic won’t do.
paragraphs: Importing product data does not rewrite your listings. Publishing requires a chosen action. Models decide what to recommend; a simulation cannot promise a future sale.

sections.title: We publish what we ask you to publish.
sections.description: ecentic’s own llms.txt, API catalog, OAuth discovery, agent checkout profile and MCP endpoint are public. The REST API is versioned and documented in OpenAPI 3.1, and the CLI runs with npx @ecentic/cli.
sections.note: Current developer interfaces support discovery and onboarding, not dashboard results export.

faqs.question: Do I need all five steps?
faqs.answer: No. You can start with Connect and Simulate, then decide which products need changes.

faqs.question: Which platforms work today?
faqs.answer: Shopify and WooCommerce connect directly. Compatible product feeds and CSV files support imports from other systems.

faqs.question: Is a simulation the same as live AI traffic?
faqs.answer: No. It is a controlled comparison against named competitors. Detected live AI referrals are measured separately on Shopify.

faqs.question: Where do I see prices?
faqs.answer: See the Pricing page. Enterprise pilots are scoped on a call.

faqs.question: Does ecentic publish anything on its own?
faqs.answer: The current listing flow requires an explicit Apply action, including any bulk action you choose. Structured data and Merchant Center sync have separate controls.

faqs.question: What exactly gets written?
faqs.answer: Listing Apply writes the title and description. Structured data is published separately. Shopify stores can send published fixes to Merchant Center with a separate sync. Prices and stock are not rewritten by the listing action.

faqs.question: Is the lift you show measured?
faqs.answer: It is an estimate per fix. A new scan lets you compare a later set of simulated decisions. It is not a measurement of added sales.

faqs.question: Will it change our brand voice?
faqs.answer: The rewrite starts from existing product facts. Apply generates and publishes it, so choose that action only when you are ready for the listing to change. There is no generated-copy preview step today.

faqs.question: Do we need to change payment providers?
faqs.answer: The WooCommerce flow uses your store’s gateway. Supported instruments and any shopper handoff depend on the gateway and configuration; test the exact flow before enabling it.

faqs.question: Does Shopify already handle agent checkout?
faqs.answer: Shopify controls its own channel eligibility and checkout infrastructure. ecentic’s Shopify features focus on product comparisons, listing changes, tracking and supported Merchant Center checks. Check current eligibility on the channel pages.

faqs.question: Can AI buy from us inside ChatGPT?
faqs.answer: We have not confirmed publication of the ecentic ChatGPT app, so it is marked Coming soon. The ChatGPT channel page explains the currently verified merchant routes.

faqs.question: Which AI channels support buying today?
faqs.answer: Each channel has its own eligibility and payment rules. Our channel pages show dated sources and distinguish ecentic’s implemented features from planned connectors.

faqs.question: Does tracking work on WooCommerce?
faqs.answer: Not yet. The visit-tracking installation runs on Shopify today.

faqs.question: How is an order AI-attributed?
faqs.answer: Pay-as-you-go first accepts an explicit attribution tag if available. Otherwise it looks for a recent AI referral anywhere in that store within the configured window, seven days by default. This does not establish that the same shopper made the order.

faqs.question: Can we export tracking data through the API?
faqs.answer: Not through the current public API, MCP server or CLI. These interfaces cover discovery and onboarding workflows; visit data is available in the dashboard.
